text.p: These are the leading stories in the Skopje press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The oldest and most prominent daily in Macedonia Nova Makedonija was registered in the Skopje municipal court as a joint venture company. Pande Kolemisevski, former editor-in-chief, was appointed the president of the Board of Directors.
- Nova Makedonija blames the government for not informing the public about the U.S. SECI initiative and for failing to consult the opposition on crucial national issues.

- The political situation in Tetovo became more complicated after a fight between the PDP and PDPA election observers at a polling post on Sunday. The two ethnic Albanian parties blame eachother for violence and obstructions to the electoral process. The Macedonian Democratic Party calls for a meeting of all party leaders in Tetovo to try to resolve the crisis.

- Following the events in Tetovo, president of the State electoral commission Liljana Ingilizova says the "local elections should be finally terminated. A solution for Tetovo will be find within the law."
- The capital, Skopje, suffocates in smog as concentration of air pollution is three times higher than allowed.
